title: board-declutter — the AI board loses its chrome: one quiet line on top, cards with a background, a rail on a border

set.request: this ai dashboard has way too much bullshit. 1) there's like... 200px of dead space at the top. 2) Todays' board? Everything? Process? Start here? V3? 103 left? days, now, grid, timeline, prompts, gallery, dashboard, LIVE, everyone, card width -- then under that, minion-alpha-writer - minion - idle, minion-beta-writer - minion - idle, .etc... then the rail has a bunch of padding on the top, and the rail's scrollbar is literally hovering. scrollbars should be at the edge of a clear border. in this case, it should be full height, spanning the entire workspace (minus the header). the ui cards don't have bgs. they should have lightened (but not white) bg, and the selected card should turn white. ADDENDUM: the timeline, prompts, grid, now, and days, don't even have a route... a live reload would navigate me away from this page... the tabs seem to use some sort of localstorage to persist the current tab... but that's literally what routes are for.
steps: Measure before: dead space, chrome rows, chips, rail padding/height, card bg, at 1280/400/1920
Deliverable 6: every view is a URL (routes beat localStorage)
Deliverable 2+3: one quiet chrome line, More fold, idle agents collapse to a count
Deliverable 1: kill the dead space at the cause
Deliverable 4: the rail on a border, full height, no top padding
Deliverable 5: card backgrounds lightened, selected turns white
Measure after + screenshots at three widths
Deliverable 8: hide the grid behind one flag, its url redirects
Deliverable 9: nothing touches the rail, and the head gap goes
set.outcome:
**The grid is hidden, nothing on the board touches the rail any more, the gap above the chrome line is gone — and the blank page you got when you clicked a view word was mine, found and fixed.**

**Why a view word went blank.** `Router.go()` loads first and pushes the url second, on purpose — a failed navigation should leave no history entry. So while a page builds itself on a real in-app click, `location.pathname` is still the url you are leaving, and the check I added this morning to stop the board drawing itself twice saw a mismatch and drew nothing at all. Every cold load passed, which is exactly why it shipped. Every page on the board now draws one tick later, when the url is certainly final.

Walking in from three different places — not just loading urls cold — turned up two more blank paths: arriving at `/framework/ai/` from a first click in the same tab (a sibling agent hit that from your 18:18 report and patched it; their fix stands), and clicking **AI** in the rail from a day page. That last one could not be fixed by any handoff, because the day has its own `page.js` outside this board. So a page now watches its own element for the class that says it is the one being shown, and draws then — one observer, and it let five hooks be deleted.

**The grid is hidden, not deleted.** One flag, `HIDDEN_VIEWS`. Its word is off the line; `/framework/ai/grid/`, `?view=grid` and a saved preference reading "grid" all land on days and rewrite themselves there, so nothing you have ever linked or bookmarked goes nowhere. Taking the word out of that array brings the whole view back.

**Nothing touches the rail.** The "sorted by importance…" line was the one thing on the board with no padding at all — `.v3-wall` is `display: contents`, so every child has to claim the page gutter for itself and that line never did. It sat at 0.0px from the rail's border at every width; it is at 15.1px at 1280 and 62.1px at 3440 now, the same gutter every card stands on. Every other view already had it.

**The gap above the chrome line is gone.** It was `--pad`, which is a percentage of the containing block, so the empty grey above the title grew with the screen: 15.0px at 1280 and **62.1px at 3440**. Sideways the row still stands on the page gutter; downwards it now takes its own em — 9.0px at 1280, 8.4px at 400, 10.8px at 3440. Dead space above the first card: **202.4 → 61.6px** at 1280.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| dead space above the first card (1280) | 202.4px | 61.6px |
| space above the chrome line (1280 / 3440) | 15.0 / 62.1px | 9.0 / 10.8px |
| the "sorted by…" line, from the rail | 0.0px | 15.1px at 1280, 62.1px at 3440 |
| view words on the line | 7, two greyed and dead | 4 — grid behind one flag |
| clicking a view word | blank page | one board, every time |

**Left open, and why:** the usage footer's own text sits 13px from the rail at 1280 rather than 15.1 — `--pad`'s floor is one em of the box it is in, and that strip is typed a step smaller, so 13px IS its own gutter. Forcing the page ramp onto a control strip is the mistake the size standard exists to prevent. The hour dividers in the timeline still bleed their boxes to the column edge on purpose; their text is at the gutter.
